newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Junior minister nabbed in Russian tax crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Junior minister nabbed in Russian tax crackdown.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is to sack a junior minister in his own government for not paying his taxes, Russian media said on Tuesday.

Vadim Kisin, deputy minister for relations with the Commonwealth of Independent States, is an early victim of the Temporary Emergency Commission (VChK) set up to crack down on tax dodgers, whom Chernomyrdin blames for shaky state finances.

"Tomorrow he will be relieved of the post he occupies for concealing income and non-payment of taxes," Chernomyrdin was quoted as saying by Itar-Tass news agency after a meeting of the commission he jointly heads.
"It will be the same for everyone."

A massive shortfall in tax collection has, the government says, been the reason for unpaid pensions and public sector wages. The International Monetary Fund is withholding the latest tranche of a $10 billion loan over concerns on state revenues.

Chernomyrdin was quoted as calling undeclared income and hidden wealth as "a real black hole" for funds that ought to be flowing in the state coffers. He said the government planned a range of measures to stamp it out.
